subject: problems estimating scale of multivariate prior for hierarchical regression

messages.author: 3f37be0cf708d442
messages.subject: problems estimating scale of multivariate prior for hierarchical regression
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to estimate an I believe straight forward hierarchical logistic regression, but the traces for some parameters (mainly tau, the coefficient scales of the multivariate hierarchical prior ) look “spiky” (see attached figure ) and I can’t seem to get the behave better. At times, these parameters also get stuck. 
The essential parts of the model are below. 
Here is what I have done so far to get nicer sampling behavior
- Reparameterized the chauchy distribution for tau (the scale of the multivariate priors) as described on pages 198-190 in the stan reference
- Increased the sampler parameter max_treedepth  to 15
- Increased target acceptance rate to .9 and jittered stepsize (.5)
All this has all little effect (If anything, the results with the modified parameters are worse).

I am attaching traceplots and histograms of acceptance probability, step size, treedepth.

So I basically have three questions now:
1) Does the sample trace look OK after all, and I am worrying for nothing?
2) Are the modified sampler parameters I used OK, or should I use different parameter values?
3) Does the model look all right?

The full model and a small data set are attached. (Full model and data are attached. Note that the full model has lots of code to scale variables and to prepare and do average predictive comparisons)

Cheers - Guido


############# essential sections of the model #################

parameters {
  // covariances for regression model parameters for mean of negative binomial
  // (from stan language reference)
  matrix[K,M] z;
  cholesky_factor_corr[K] L_Omega; 
  //vector<lower=0>[K] tau;           // prior scale
  vector<lower=0, upper=pi()/2>[K] tau_unif;
  matrix[L,K] gamma;                // group coeffs
  
}
transformed parameters {
  // regression weights for mean of negative binomial model
  vector<lower=0>[K] tau;
  matrix[M,K] beta;
  for (k in 1:K) tau[k] <- tan(tau_unif[k]);
  beta <- gx * gamma + (diag_pre_multiply(tau,L_Omega) * z)';
}
model {
  // log(mean) of negative binomial
  vector[N] alpha;

  // sample parameters
  //tau ~ cauchy(0,2.5); # orig scale = 2.5
  to_vector(z) ~ normal(0,1);
  L_Omega ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(2);
  to_vector(gamma) ~ normal(0,5); # orig scale = 5
  
  alpha <- to_vector(sx * beta');

  // increment binomial
  y ~ bernoulli_logit(alpha);

}

########### model calls ################
called the model with 
stanfit = stan(file = "stanmodels/HLRegP/HLRegressionP.stan",data = standata,chains = 1, iter = 500, control=list(refresh = 25))
and 
stanfit_plus = stan(fit = stanfit,data = standata,chains = 4, iter = 500,control = list(max_treedepth = 15, adapt_delta = .85, stepsize_jitter = .25))
(I a longer warmup, i tried 750, does not make a difference)

I am attaching the plots for tau_unif and for tau for a new run.

the prior for tau_unif was on purpose a uniform. I omitted the sampling statement because the variable will be samples as a from a uniform with the boundaries specified during variable declaration. For the sake o clarity  I should have included the sampling statement.

following the stan reference i replaced 
chauchy(0,1)
with 
tan_unif<lower=0,uper=pi/2>
tau <- tan(tan_unif)

(the example in stan reference is to substitute beta ~ chauchy(mu,tau) with beta_unif<lower = -pi()/2,upper = pi(2)> and beta <- mu + tau*tan(beta_unif)

cheers - guido
